analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (2 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities fell on Friday: S&P 500 -1.82%, Nasdaq -2.86% (worst session since June), Dow -1.09%. Breadth was only slightly negative and equal-weight RSP outperformed the cap-weighted index by about 100 bp. The AI trade was the biggest drag, with semis, memory and neoclouds sharply lower.

Treasuries rallied on flight-to-safety buying, with yields down 2-8 bp. Gold fell 3.3% (worst day since June, back below $4K), bitcoin futures lost 5.2% after the Binance hack, and WTI crude rose 2.1% on skepticism about a diplomatic offramp in Iran.

Light US data day: Q3 ECI +0.8% m/m, in line with consensus. October Chicago PMI printed 55.3 against 56.0 consensus, with prices paid at the highest since December 2021. October payrolls are due next Friday, expected at +40K.

Post-FOMC Fedspeak stayed firm. Dallas Fed's Logan said two more 25 bp hikes are needed before pausing. St. Louis Fed's Musalem said rates may need to rise again soon. Rate path pricing was modestly dovish after a less-hawkish policy assessment.

Amazon fell after earnings. AWS growth of 39% beat but missed elevated buyside expectations. Q3 capex of $77B was about $20B above consensus, TTM FCF was -$42B, and management plans to spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Retail and advertising slowed and missed, and Q4 operating income guidance was below consensus at the midpoint. Bull points: AWS growth projected at 40%+ in 2027 and 2028, backlog of $578B.

Intel fell 28.6%. Q3 EPS beat but revenue missed, with Client Computing revenue down 5.1% y/y to $8.1B against a $8.95B consensus. Q4 EPS and revenue guidance came in well below the Street. Intel expects the PC market to fall 10% in 2027 after a 12% decline this year, citing memory shortages and high component costs. Capex is $20B this year with a significant increase in 2027 and negative FCF expected. BofA downgraded to neutral from buy.

Oil rose as hopes faded for a near-term cooling of US-Iran tensions, with attention on possible renewed US strikes after next Tuesday's midterm elections. Iran's Ghalibaf demanded the US first meet preconditions (end the blockade, unfreeze assets, restart oil sales) before nuclear talks resume.

The megacap tech and semis selloff is an overhang for AI capex funding and equity raises. Alphabet is 22% below its $85B June offering price, Intel is down 33% from its $23B August offer, and buyers in Meta's $25B offering on Monday are more than 2% underwater. Anthropic's IPO is expected in November. Anthropic perpetuals on Hyperliquid are down about 25% from the 9-Sep peak.

Binance confirmed $6.3B of funds were impacted in what is described as the biggest-ever crypto hack. It froze $3B of assets and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, and said it will cover losses. TRM Labs attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit. Tether and Circle froze $2.54B of linked assets.

US earnings movers: CPRI +16.3%, FDXF +14.9%, REGN +13.3% on a big Q3 beat, GPN +13% on take-private talks, COIN -10.6%, SNDK -13.5%, TWLO -15.2%, RBLX -18.1%, ILMN -18.6%, RDDT -29.2% on a DAUq miss, ATEC -38.1%.
Europe was mixed: DAX -0.9%, FTSE 100 +0.1%, CAC unchanged, STOXX 600 -0.4%. Renewed AI-capex worries hit tech. Bund yield fell 4 bp to 3.33% and gilts fell 2 bp to 5.28%.

The ECB held rates but takeaways point to a December hike unless activity slows notably, followed by a pause. Lagarde said a hike was discussed and stressed upside inflation risk. ECB staff estimate higher bond yields cut growth by a cumulative 100 bps and inflation by 90 bps in 2027-28 versus the September baseline. Lagarde will step down on 7-Feb.

Preliminary October euro-area national inflation diverged: Germany 2.8% y/y (from 3.3%), France 3.4% (from 3.1%), Italy 5.4% (from 4.2%, consensus 4.6%), Spain 4.9% unchanged. Pantheon raised its Eurozone October inflation forecast to 4% ahead of the 4-Nov flash HICP.

UK: the Budget was low-key and the OBR cut 2027 growth to 1.0% from 1.6%. Markets price over 90% odds of a 25 bp BoE hike to 4% next week and about 50% for a December move, with a 6-3 vote split tipped. BoE DMP year-ahead firm inflation expectations rose to 3.3% from 3.1%.

STOXX 600 Q3 earnings (43% reported) are growing 35.8% y/y against 18.9% expected, with Energy driving most of it (+135.7%). Ex-Energy growth is about 17%. Aggregate sales surprise is -2.13%. JPMorgan has 2027 STOXX 600 EPS growth slowing to +9.5%.

Asia: Nikkei -2.12%, Hang Seng +1.46%, Shanghai -1.44%. Tech fell sharply, Taiwan's Taiex hit two-month lows near a correction, and MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan is 6.6% lower for the month. Defensives and alternatives gained at AI's expense.

The BOJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote (Takata dissented for a 25 bp hike), said underlying inflation is consistent with 2%, and flagged another hike as likely. It surprised markets by raising ETF sales to about 0.1% of trading value from 0.05% (JPY860B per year versus JPY330B), starting January 2027. FY27 core inflation forecast was raised to 2.6% from 2.4%.

Samsung Electronics posted record Q3 operating profit of KRW107T, in line with its preliminary figure, but net profit of KRW75T missed the KRW86.1T consensus and no new shareholder return plan was announced. It guided to a deeper chip shortage next year, double-digit foundry revenue growth in Q4, and capex up almost 60% to KRW84.4T versus KRW74.4T consensus. Shares fell about 6%.

South Korea September industrial output rose 9.0% m/m, the strongest since February 2009, led by a 19.2% rise in semis (DRAM). Japan September industrial production rose 2.2% m/m versus 1.2% consensus, while retail sales fell 0.7% m/m versus +0.3% expected.

market_movers.rationale: BofA downgraded to neutral from buy, citing lack of traction with external foundry customers and a sharp PC shipment decline.
Canaccord Genuity downgraded to hold from buy, citing softer legacy markets with no timeline on recovery.
Citi upgraded Snam to hold, viewing lower 2027 regulated returns as temporary and largely reversing in 2028.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Haleon to hold, citing weak H2 growth from structural channel shifts and poor execution.
Vontobel downgraded Sandoz to hold after a Q3 sales miss, seeing no remaining upside.
DNB downgraded Boliden to hold, saying the 17% Q3 EBIT beat reflected lower-quality items and 2028 estimates fall.
Berenberg downgraded Wacker Chemie to hold on limited 2027 EBITDA growth and Section 232 uncertainty. Deutsche Bank downgraded to sell, with 2027-29 estimates about 7% below consensus.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Aixtron to buy, citing Q3 orders more than doubling y/y to EUR275M on optoelectronics demand and an earlier power recovery.

sector_views.rationale: Software, networking, tech hardware, semis, memory and neoclouds led the declines on AI capex and funding concerns.
Energy, staples, pharma/biotech, insurers and exchanges outperformed in the US selloff.
Food & Beverage, Health Care, Personal & Household Goods and Media outperformed, while Basic Resources, Technology and Banks lagged.

earnings_insights: AMZN Q3 (reported): AWS growth 39%, capex $77B (about $20B above consensus), TTM FCF -$42B, Q4 operating income guidance below consensus at the midpoint, AWS backlog $578B.

INTC Q3 (reported): EPS beat (adjusted basis not specified), revenue missed. Client Computing revenue $8.1B (-5.1% y/y) versus $8.95B consensus. Q4 EPS and revenue guided below the Street. Israeli factory shutdown expected to cut revenue by $600M over two quarters.
RDDT Q3 (reported): revenue, EPS and EBITDA beat, DAUq missed, and Q4 revenue/EBITDA guidance came in below consensus. Management warned DAUs could decline low-double-digits.
REGN Q3 (reported): big EPS and revenue beat on US Eylea net sales growth and Sanofi collaboration revenue. FY gross margin guidance raised.
COIN Q3 (reported): adjusted EBITDA beat on USDC and staking revenue. Prediction markets passed a $200M annualized revenue run rate, while spot volumes and transaction revenue stayed pressured.
SNDK F1Q (reported): EPS and revenue beat with F2Q guidance above consensus. An 8-for-1 stock split was announced.
TWLO Q3 (reported): revenue, EPS and OI beat with 16% organic growth. FY26 guidance raised. Preliminary FY27 organic growth of at least 10% was below bullish expectations.
RBLX Q3 (reported): bookings and DAUs beat, Q4 bookings and EBITDA guidance below consensus on AI infrastructure and marketing investment.
ILMN Q3 (reported): EPS beat, revenue light, FY26 EPS and revenue guidance raised. Shares were up 121% YTD into the print.
SYK Q3 (reported): EPS missed, revenue light, FY26 EPS and organic growth guidance cut.
PINS Q3 (reported): revenue and EBITDA missed, MAUs a record 661M (+10% y/y). Q4 guidance below consensus on European cross-border advertiser weakness.
FDXF (reported four months to 30-Sep): EPS $2.15, revenue $3.30B, with transition-period guidance raised.
SAN-FR Q3 (reported): business operating income EUR5.43B versus EUR4.32B consensus. Sales growth forecast raised to low-teens from 10%.
AZN-GB Q3 (reported): revenue $16.2B (+7% CER, 2% above consensus), Core EPS $2.79 (9% ahead). FY2026 guidance unchanged.
BP-GB Q3 (reported): net income $8.5B, underlying cash flow $14.3B, net debt $13.9B.
NWG-GB Q3 (reported): adjusted PBT missed consensus by 1%, CET1 13.5%.
Samsung Electronics Q3 (reported): operating profit KRW107T (in line), net profit KRW75T versus KRW86.1T consensus, semiconductor profit KRW106.5T versus KRW108.5T consensus.

STOXX 600 Q3 (43% reported): earnings growth 35.8% y/y (blended 26.3%) versus 18.9% expected at season start. Aggregate earnings surprise +2.85%, sales surprise -2.13%. Consensus Q4 growth +30.5%, FY2026 +21.8%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with consensus, so no new wage-inflation signal.
Slight miss, but prices paid were the highest since December 2021.
Consensus expectation for the report due next Friday.
Markets price over 90% odds, with a 6-3 vote split tipped and about 50% odds of a December move.

macro_indicators.reading: December hike expected, then a pause
macro_indicators.interpretation: Based on ECB takeaways and Bloomberg/Reuters sources, a hike follows unless activity slows markedly.
Fell more than expected as a temporary fuel tax cut slowed energy price growth.
Sharpest jump among the large euro-area economies.
Pantheon sees a low bar for a December ECB hike. Flash release due 4-Nov.
Held in an 8-1 vote. BOJ flagged another hike as likely.
Beat, led by autos, production equipment and business machinery.
Downside surprise, with tourism spending a weak spot.
Strongest since February 2009, driven by DRAM.
Growth forecast was cut, but the gilt reaction was muted.
Rising, with no sign of wage pass-through.

crypto_views: Binance confirmed $6.3B of funds impacted by a suspected hack, the biggest ever. $3B of assets were frozen and withdrawals were suspended temporarily.
Tether and Circle together froze $2.54B of assets linked to the incident. TRM Labs attributed it to North Korea's TraderTraitor.
Bitcoin futures fell 5.2%. Coinbase said it was unaffected but is monitoring, and the report notes discussion of risk to investor confidence and liquidity.
Pre-IPO Anthropic perpetual contracts on Hyperliquid trade at their lowest since mid-August, down about 25% from the 9-Sep peak.

Coinbase Q3: prediction markets passed a $200M annualized revenue run rate, subscription/services revenue was stronger on USDC and staking, and market share rose for a fourth straight quarter despite weak crypto trading.
risk_factors: AI capex funding strain: hyperscaler capex above consensus, negative FCF at Amazon and Intel, and big equity offerings trading below issue price.
Equity supply from the expected Anthropic IPO in November, potentially larger than SpaceX's.
Anthropic's $63B chip financing deal is expected to receive a high junk rating after the IPO (per Blackstone).
Renewed US strikes on Iran after the midterms, with upside risk to oil.
Crypto exchange security and confidence after the Binance hack.
Central bank tightening: Fed officials signalling more hikes, a likely ECB December hike and a BoE hike next week.
Memory shortages and component costs hitting PC demand (Intel expects the PC market to fall 10% in 2027).
BOJ ETF selling accelerating from January 2027 could compound pessimism in a downturn (MUFG Trust Bank).
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index at 19.42, up 12.91% on the day.
Short-closing provided a small boost into the Asian close.
Equal-weight RSP outperformed the cap-weighted S&P 500 by about 100 bp, with breadth only slightly negative.
Taiwan's Taiex ended at two-month lows and near a technical correction.
geopolitical: US-Iran tensions: hopes for diplomacy are fading and the Trump administration appears to be planning a new round of strikes after the midterm elections. CENTCOM commander Cooper briefed Trump in person.
Iran demands that the US end the blockade, unfreeze assets and restart oil sales before nuclear talks resume. Qatari negotiators are in Tehran.
North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking unit was identified by TRM Labs as behind the Binance theft.
UK is drawing up off-balance-sheet funding plans for defense spending, with a 3% of GDP target by 2030, and is in talks with at least three NATO members about an international financing bank.
US midterm elections are next Tuesday, and Acerinox cited US uncertainty ahead of them.
China tourism to Japan more than halved after the diplomatic spat over PM Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan.
cross_bank_references: BofA downgraded Intel to neutral from buy.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Haleon to hold, downgraded Wacker Chemie to sell, and upgraded Aixtron to buy.
Berenberg downgraded Wacker Chemie to hold.
JPMorgan has 2027 STOXX 600 EPS growth slowing to +9.5%.
Pantheon raised its Eurozone October inflation forecast to 4%.
